title: Turning Interaction History into Execution State: A Runtime Layer for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
event_hint: Ledger deterministic execution-state layer prevents stale reads and redundant commands
problem: Long-horizon coding agents accumulate hundreds of actions and observations but do not explicitly track which reads remain valid after edits or which commands repeat completed work. Reconstructing execution status from raw history can cause stale-file reasoning, duplicate reads/tests, and unnecessary cost.
mechanism: Ledger maintains a deterministic online execution ledger of verified observations, repository modifications, and attempted commands. Its inform path appends a compact current-state view before each model decision; its govern path checks proposed commands before execution, reuses still-valid earlier results, or flags/suppresses likely redundant repetition. It adds no model calls and wraps an otherwise unmodified agent.

evidence.claim: Across all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, Ledger raised Pass@1 from 56.2% to 64.2% with GPT-5 mini and from 75.8% to 81.0% with MiniMax M2.5.
Ledger reduced total cost by 28.9% for GPT-5 mini and 31.8% for MiniMax M2.5.
Attached to OpenAI Codex, Ledger added 3.4 percentage points of Pass@1 while reducing total cost by 24.4%.
evidence.condition: Transfer experiment on a second agent scaffold

evidence.claim: The inform path primarily drives efficiency gains, while the govern path drives most resolution gains; their combination performs best.
Observation records are created only for successful, untruncated single-file reads and retain local/global modification counters to determine whether the observation remains current.
evidence.baseline: Raw command history without validity state

evaluation_context: Ledger was evaluated on all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances using two model backbones (GPT-5 mini and MiniMax M2.5) and two agent scaffolds (mini-swe-agent and OpenAI Codex). It is integrated without modifying the base agent or adding LLM calls; metrics include Pass@1 and total cost.
limitations: The excerpt does not report tool-call counts, duplicate-read counts, wall-clock latency, or the absolute cost distribution, so cost reductions cannot be attributed to each command type. Ledger's validity logic is conservative and relies on detectable file modifications; external side effects, generated files, shell state, or semantic changes not reflected in tracked counters may remain ambiguous. Results cover SWE-bench Verified and two specific models/scaffolds, not arbitrary long-horizon workflows (inference).
project_relevance: This is a direct runtime pattern for reducing repeated Read/Grep/test work: persist verified observations and modification counters, inject a compact state before delegation, and gate execution before re-running commands. It supports bounded sub-agent contracts by allowing the parent to distinguish fresh evidence from stale or already-completed work without extra model calls; acceptance should measure duplicate tool calls, token cost, correctness, and invalidation behavior (inference).
